title: UNC/UNF Thread Coverage Expansion

provenance_sources.source: Definitional: Unified numbered screw gauge formula (major_diameter = 0.060in + gauge_number x 0.013in) for numbered sizes; fractional designation = nominal diameter for fractional sizes; TPI is literally part of every ASME B1.1 thread designation.
provenance_sources.corroborating_source: Yamawa Co. (tap/threading tool manufacturer) technical reference No.078, explicitly deriving and confirming the numbered-gauge formula; AmesWeb's UNC thread chart, which cites ASME B1.1-2003 directly for its major-diameter/TPI table.
provenance_sources.reasoning: Not a variable engineering recommendation — the diameter/TPI relationship is fixed by the designation system itself and confirmed by an unambiguous, internally-consistent formula from an industry manufacturer's technical reference, not from chart agreement alone.

provenance_sources.source: faculty.etsu.edu tap-drill reference chart (university-hosted, single coherent table covering all 9 target sizes)
provenance_sources.cross_validation: Every value was cross-checked against the T2-verified Machinery's Handbook thread-engagement formula (% = (Dmajor-Ddrill)/(1.29904*P)*100, ~75% engagement basis) before acceptance. All 9 values are formula-consistent (drill diameter matches the nearest stocked drill size to the formula's calculated ~75%-engagement diameter).
provenance_sources.reasoning: No Tier 1 primary standard table (ASME B94.9's own tables) was obtainable in this phase — the ANSI/ASME preview page returned HTTP 403 unlike the ISO 2306 preview in T2.1. Formula cross-validation provides meaningful corroboration beyond simple chart agreement, but does not constitute primary-source verification.

provenance_sources.field_group: hex_head_in, clearance_hole_close_in, clearance_hole_normal_in, clearance_hole_loose_in (all 9 new records)
provenance_sources.reasoning: These fields are not tapping-domain-relevant (general fastener/hardware geometry) and no verified source was independently obtained. Hex-head format is also atypical for numbered machine-screw sizes (#4 through #10) in common fastener practice. Left null rather than populated from unverified commercial charts.

rejected_value_notes.reason: Fails cross-check against the Machinery's Handbook engagement formula by a wide margin (formula predicts ~0.114in, not 0.1457in). Likely an aggregation/transcription error in the search summary, not a legitimate alternate convention. Demonstrates why formula cross-validation, not source-count agreement, is the governing check.
Same as above (formula predicts ~0.451in; the value used, 0.4531in from a coherent single-source chart, matches).

iso_2306_alternative_drill_structural_ad.description: All 15 UNC/UNF tapping_profile records (6 pre-existing from T1 + 9 new from T2.1a) now carry a structured `iso_2306_alternative_drill` field alongside `hole_preparation`, recording ISO 2306:1972's own metric drill-diameter recommendation for the same thread as a distinct, separately-labeled, independently-verified (against the primary ISO 2306 table obtained in T2.1) value. Neither field overrides, averages with, or is treated as superseding the other.

iso_2306_alternative_drill.convention: ISO 2306 continuous-metric recommendation for inch threads

unresolved_fields: hex_head_in and 3 clearance_hole_*_in fields remain unavailable (null) on all 9 new base-thread records.
tap_drill_in on all 9 new records remains source_bound, not verified — no Tier 1 primary table (ASME B94.9) was obtainable.

source_conflicts.description: 4 WebSearch-aggregated tap-drill values for UNF sizes were found to conflict with the formula-consistent, single-source chart values and were rejected (see rejected_value_notes). This is a same-claim conflict (not a different-standard conflict like T2.1's UNC/UNF-vs-ISO2306 finding) — one candidate value was simply wrong.
source_conflicts.resolution_method: Cross-validation against the independently T2-verified thread-engagement formula, not vote-counting or source-count agreement.
